name: three-rs-one-behavior
title: The Three R’s, One Behavior at a Time
part: Built the same way: one behavior at a time
kicker: How it was built · the same R’s, at the smallest scale
html:
The Three R’s, One Behavior at a Time

One behaviorComponents and the system
Gherkin says what right means before the code existsOnly the acts the state allows; a reason when not
The scenario runs the same way on every changeA kept script replays the same way, with no model
A break goes red, and the gate refuses the commit, even the model’sBuster tampers on purpose; ARTIE takes the right failure path

One test at a time, for components and systems that are themselves right, repeatable and resilient.
say: Recall the three R's: right behavior, repeatability, resilience. We've been measuring the running system against them. Now let's look at how it was built, because it's the same three, at the smallest scale there is: one behavior at a time. A Gherkin scenario says what right behavior means, in words a person can read, before any code exists. A red run proves the scenario can fail, and catches the behavior missing. Then the code, then a green run, then a gated commit. That's right behavior. Now that scenario runs the same way on every change, forever: that's repeatability. And when the next change breaks it, the suite goes red and the gate refuses the commit, even when the model wrote the change: that's resilience. Do that one behavior at a time, a few thousand times, and you get generic components, ARTIE, the gateway, heart-mcp, Buster, that are themselves right, repeatable and resilient. Put those together and you get a system with the same three properties. Same R's, from one test all the way up to a real merge on GitHub. The next few slides show how the gates make that hold while nobody's watching.

deck:ref.name: right-behavior
deck:ref.label: RIGHT-BEHAVIOR
deck:ref.title: Right behavior: only what the state allows, and a reason when not
deck:ref.summary: The agent is offered only the acts the current state allows, sends each one with the validator from the state it read, and gets a reason when an act is absent. At the small scale it is a Gherkin scenario that says what right means before any code is written.

deck:ref.name: repeatability
deck:ref.label: REPEATABILITY
deck:ref.title: Repeatability: the same goal, the same result, every time
deck:ref.summary: Given the same inputs, the same outputs, call after call. Found once with a model, then replayed with none: the same steps, the same checks, the same result, until the controls really change. At the small scale it is one scenario that runs the same way every time.

deck:ref.name: resilience
deck:ref.label: RESILIENCE
deck:ref.title: Resilience: the server changes, the client doesn't break
deck:ref.summary: When the server changes, or misbehaves on purpose, the client takes the failure path the spec names, re-syncs, and goes on; a model comes back only when the controls really changed, to repair. At the small scale it is the regression suite and the gates that hold, even against the model.
